newsitem.title: USA: Va. Power restarts North Anna 1 nuclear plant.
newsitem.headline: Va. Power restarts North Anna 1 nuclear plant.

text.p: Virginia Power Co restarted the 911 megawatt (MW) North Anna 1 nuclear unit after an electrical problem automatically tripped it off line early Thursday, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said.
North Anna 1 was producing at 12 percent of capacity late Thursday, the NRC said in its daily status report.
The company said Thursday it had not yet set a startup date for the unit.
While investigating the cause of North Anna 1's shutdown, the company also examined a high pressure turbine balance pipe for any signs of corrosion.
In its report, the NRC noted the neighboring 909 MW North Anna unit 2 will begin the restart process after unit 1 hits 30 percent power.
Virginia Power, a subsidiary of Dominion Resources, is the operator and has an 88.4 percent stake in North Anna complex, while Old Dominion Electric Co-operative holds the remaining 11.6 percent.
The North Anna facility produces roughly 17 percent of Virginia Power's annual electricity output.
